text:
incident-bot: Pager: sev2 — increased 5xx rate and routing errors observed for /v1/generate across eu clusters. SmartRouting flagged fallback loop between eu-west1 and us-west2. Paging oncall: @eve-sre :rotating_light:

alice: seeing ~18% 5xx from europe for the last 7m, latency spikes too. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/boards/smartroute-prod — spike aligns with DNS prop window.

ben: looks like requests from eu are being routed to us-west, then back to eu, TTL mismatch maybe? also noticed a model variant mismatch — some requests are hitting gptx-small instead of gptx-medium (quality regressions reported by support).

carla: confirmed in logs. excerpt from router logs: `route_decision: smart-route fallback -> region: eu-west1 -> fallback: us-west2 -> model_variant: gptx-small` — should have fallen back to gptx-medium.

dmitri: @carla can you grep for the policy id and config timestamp? I want to see if a config rollout touched variant mappings.

carla: policy_id=sr-prod-v2, last_deploy=1945674300, modified_by=deploy-bot. config snippet: ```yaml
policies:
  - id: sr-prod-v2
    failover_sequence:
      - region: eu-west1
      - region: us-west2
    variant_fallback: true
    variant_map:
      default: gptx-medium
      fallback: gptx-small  # <-- this looks wrong, fallback should be gptx-medium for capacity-only fallbacks
```

alice: ohhh. deploy-bot recent change set default->medium but fallback->small. That explains quality regressions. How did DNS propagation create a loop though?

ben: edge DNS in eu-west had stale rrset for a subset of VIPs (some nodes removed but old endpoints still cached at several resolvers). SmartRouting saw some endpoints healthy and some not, flipped across regions; combined with variant_fallback=true it kept oscillating and hitting small.

incident-bot: timeline: first anomaly 1945678520, config deploy 1945674300, DNS anomaly detected 1945678400 by edge-monitor. Impact: ~12% of production traffic for eu region sees wrong variant + 2x latency. Several enterprise customers reported degraded responses.

carla: mitigation plan: 1) disable variant_fallback in sr-prod-v2 2) pin model variant to gptx-medium for eu region 3) force DNS cache purge / reduce TTLs for affected rrsets 4) monitor 5xx/latency and customer-reported regressions.

eve-sre: taking lead. executing steps now.

ops-bot: runbook action logged by @eve-sre: disable_variant_fallback sr-prod-v2 -> ACCEPTED.

eve-sre: ran `redwoodctl smartroute update --id sr-prod-v2 --set variant_fallback=false` — patch applied, rolling.

carla: pin command to set variant: ```bash
redwoodctl smartroute set-variant --policy sr-prod-v2 --region eu-west1 --variant gptx-medium
```

eve-sre: pinned. now forcing DNS refresh for eu-west edge: ```bash
kubectl exec -n edge-tools dns-flusher -- /usr/local/bin/purge_rrset --vip vip-eu-01
# also triggered cloud-dns cache purge via provider API
```

ben: watching graphs — within 90s we see failover oscillation dampening. 5xx dropping from 18% -> 3% and latency percentiles improving.

alice: support notified: CS sent proactive messages to affected customers and opened tickets for those who reported quality hits.

dmitri: followups to investigate: why did deploy-bot push fallback->small? Was it a manual override or CI regression? Also audit resolver caches that had stale entries — some third-party resolvers kept old rrsets for >TTL.

carla: gathering logs for postmortem. pulling router traces and dns resolver responses: `tcpdump -n -vvv -i eth0 port 53` + router trace request ids.

eve-sre: rolling handoff in 30m to @ben for monitoring and postmortem ownership. I'll stay available for 1:1 if needed.

incident-bot: oncall_handoff scheduled 1945680200 — new owner ben.

ben: I'll own the postmortem and remediation items. immediate actions: revert deploy-bot config pipeline gating so variant_map changes require a manual approval, add an automated check that ensures fallback variants are not smaller/lower-capacity than primary for same model family.

alice: QA note — add synthetic evals across variants in eu region to detect quality drops during routing tests (fail fast).

carla: also planning DNS hygiene work: lower authoritative TTL during mass changes, and add probe cluster to sample third-party resolvers for stale rrset detection.

eve-sre: customers now seeing normal behavior, continuing close monitoring for next 2 hours. Great run — clear win for quick disable+pin approach. :thumbsup:

ben: creating incident ticket INC-194567 on Jira and assigning follow-ups (config rollback, pipeline gating, DNS probe, postmortem).

alice: postmortem owners: ben (lead), carla (routing analysis), dmitri (deploy pipeline), eve-sre (mitigation ops). ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: sev2.

eve-sre: handing over to ben now. `@ben` taking lead.

ben: ack. monitoring and will update in the incident doc.

carla: saved relevant logs to s3: s3://re/redwood/incidents/1945678901/ — will attach to Jira.

alice: thanks everyone.
